## Preliminaries

**Working scope (declared as assumption, not fact).** This final chapter is read as a single unified restoration oracle: a call to return (v1-3), the LORD's own first-person response (v4-8), and a closing wisdom colophon (v9). Assumed to bear on the inner being: Israel's called-for return and confessional speech (v1-3), the LORD's own stated turning of anger and free love (v4), the flourishing imagery applied to a restored relationship (v5-7), the LORD's direct repudiation of idols and self-identification as fruit-source (v8), and the closing wisdom framing of the whole book's ways as either walked-in or stumbled-over (v9).

**Reading rule applied.** No [AMBIGUOUS] spans in this range. One text-critical note (not a DB-flagged ambiguity but relevant to sense): v2's "pay with bulls (H6499) the vows of our lips" preserves the Masoretic reading; a well-known alternate tradition (reflected in some ancient versions) reads a homophonous form as "fruit" rather than "bulls" of the lips. The debate below follows the base extract's own rendering (bulls) as its primary reading and notes the fruit-wordplay only as a cross-reference to v8's "fruit" vocabulary, not as a competing DB-level finding.

**Corpus-continuity check.** Immediately-adjacent prior range, found automatically: `Hos 13:1-16` — `iba\app\verse-analysis\Hosea\WA-hos-13-debate.md`. Read in full before drafting this debate. Carried forward: EQ26 (ch13:14's "compassion is hidden from my eyes" vs. ch11:8-9's resolved "my compassion grows warm and tender") — this chapter's v4 ("my anger has turned from them... I will love them freely") bears directly on EQ26 and is treated as its decisive resolution within the book's own final oracle (see v4 below and Emergent questions). EQ27 (corporate guilt vs. non-culpable victims, ch13:16) is not directly addressed in ch14, which turns wholly to restoration without revisiting the ethics of ch13:16's violence; carried to the whole-book read as unresolved. EQ23 (Egypt/Assyria) is partially engaged: v3 explicitly renounces Assyria ("Assyria shall not save us") but Egypt is not named in this chapter — noted below as a partial, not full, resolution.

## Per-verse debate

### Hos 14:1

> Return, O Israel, to the Lord your God, for you have stumbled because of your iniquity.

**Observation.** Direct imperative address: "Return" (H7725G, shuv — the book's central verb) to the LORD, grounded in the stated cause: "you have stumbled [H3782] because of your iniquity [H5771G]."

**Operation 1 — call to return, grounded in named cause.**
- **Action-type:** summoned (a direct call addressed to Israel, naming both the required response and its grounding cause)
- **Subject:** Israel (second person, addressed directly)
- **Operation:** come from/go to — a called movement back toward the LORD, from a stated condition (having stumbled)
- **Source:** the prophetic voice/the LORD (issuing the call); the stumbling itself is sourced in Israel's own iniquity (self-caused, not externally imposed)
- **Target:** the LORD ("to the LORD your God")

**Interrogative — questions considered.** (Q1-Q11; every human mentioned is a presumptive candidate per step 2 note (f))
- Q1/Q2: Focused inner being — yes; "return" (shuv) is this book's own primary vocabulary for a relational/interior reorientation, not mere physical movement.
- Q3: Stated directly.
- Q4: Source of the stumbling is Israel's own iniquity (self); source of the call to return is the prophetic/divine voice.
- Q5: Target — the LORD.
- Q6: Movement (a called return) grounded in a prior state (stumbling).
- Q7: Linkage — "stumbled" (H3782) directly anticipates v9's closing "transgressors stumble [same root] in them [the LORD's ways]" — an inclusio bracketing the whole chapter (see Passage-linkages). Also reprises "return" (shuv) as the book's dominant verb, last used pointedly at ch11:5/7 (Israel's refusal to return) and now issued again as final appeal.
- Q8: Collective ("O Israel").
- Q9: Sufficient as stated.
- Q11: Action-type label — "summoned" (call to return, cause named).

**Decision.** Retain as stated IB operation — a direct call to relational reorientation, grounded in Israel's own self-caused condition.

### Hos 14:2

> Take with you words and return to the Lord; say to him, “ Take away all iniquity; accept what is good, and we will pay with bulls the vows of our lips.

**Observation.** Continued imperative: "Take with you words" (H1697G, not silver/idols as in ch13:2, but speech itself) and return; a scripted confession follows in direct quotation — request for iniquity's removal, acceptance of "what is good," and a vow ("pay... the vows of our lips," H8193G).

**Operation 1 — confessional speech offered in place of material sacrifice.**
- **Action-type:** confessed (an act of scripted, verbal self-offering, explicitly substituting words for the material objects named elsewhere in the book — silver idols ch13:2, sacrificial animals)
- **Subject:** Israel (first-person plural within the scripted speech, "we")
- **Operation:** come from/go to — words are brought (taken) as the vehicle of the return, directed toward the LORD
- **Source:** self (Israel is instructed to bring its own words, not an external offering)
- **Target:** the LORD ("say to him")

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Focused inner being — yes; the content of the confession (request for removal of iniquity, acceptance of good) is directly interior/relational.
- Q3: Stated directly, as a scripted quotation.
- Q4: Source — Israel's own words, self-generated but instructed/prescribed by the prophetic voice.
- Q5: Target — the LORD.
- Q6: Movement (words brought/return) combined with state (the request itself).
- Q7: Linkage — "words" (not silver, not idols) directly reverses ch13:2's self-financed, self-crafted idol-manufacture ("make for themselves... of their silver... the work of craftsmen") — the same self-directed resourcefulness once spent on idols is here redirected to confessional speech. The "bulls"/vows-of-lips wording also anticipates v8's "fruit" vocabulary (see Preliminaries' note on the wordplay tradition), though this debate does not adjudicate between the two readings.
- Q8: Collective ("we").
- Q9: Sufficient as stated.
- Q11: Action-type label — "confessed" (scripted, verbal, substituting for material offering).

**Decision.** Retain as stated IB operation — a genuine act of prescribed confessional speech, directly reversing the self-directed idol-manufacture of ch13:2.

### Hos 14:3

> Assyria shall not save us; we will not ride on horses; and we will say no more, ‘Our God,’ to the work of our hands. In you the orphan finds mercy.”

**Observation.** Triple renunciation within the scripted confession: Assyria will not save (H3467, same root as ch13:4's "savior" and ch13:10's rhetorical "to save you"); no reliance on horses (self-armament); no more calling the "work of our hands" (idols) "our God." Closing declaration: "In you the orphan finds mercy [H7355, racham-root]."

**Operation 1 — renunciation of the three false securities.**
- **Action-type:** renounced (a threefold, explicit rejection of alternative sources of security/help)
- **Subject:** Israel (continuing first-person plural, "we")
- **Operation:** go away — a stated turning away from three previously-relied-upon sources (political alliance, military self-reliance, idol-worship)
- **Source:** self (the renunciation is Israel's own scripted declaration)
- **Target:** Assyria, horses, and "the work of our hands" respectively — all named as objects being relinquished, not received

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Focused inner being — yes; each renunciation directly reverses an interior orientation (trust/reliance) previously misdirected, continuing the book's own diagnostic vocabulary.
- Q3: Stated directly, in the scripted confession's own words.
- Q4: Source — Israel's own renunciation, self-declared.
- Q5: Target — the three renounced objects (Assyria, horses, idols).
- Q6: Movement (turning away from) for the renunciations; state (mercy found) for the closing declaration.
- Q7: Linkage — directly answers ch13:10's rhetorical "where is your king, to save you?" and ch13:4's "besides me there is no savior" — here Israel's own confession finally affirms what the LORD asserted: no human/political power (Assyria, horses, self-armament) saves. Also: "mercy" (racham, H7355) stands in direct semantic tension with ch13:14's "compassion [nacham-root] is hidden from my eyes" — though the two Hebrew roots differ (racham vs. nacham), both belong to the same compassion/mercy semantic domain, and the movement from "hidden" (ch13:14) to "found" (ch14:3) is a significant thematic reversal, directly informing EQ26 (see below and v4).
- Q8: Collective.
- Q9: Sufficient as stated.
- Q11: Action-type label — "renounced" (threefold: political, military, religious).

**Decision.** Retain as stated IB operation — a direct, threefold renunciation of previously-diagnosed misplaced securities, closing with a mercy-declaration that bears directly on this chapter's central compassion-thread.

### Hos 14:4

> I will heal their apostasy; I will love them freely, for my anger has turned from them.

**Observation.** Three first-person declarations from the LORD: "heal" (H7495) their "apostasy" (H4878, lit. "turning away/backsliding" — the same root family as "return," shuv, used ironically of Israel's wrong turning); "love them freely" (H0157G + H5071, "freely" from a root meaning voluntary/freewill-offering — the LORD's own love described using cultic-offering vocabulary); "for my anger has turned [H7725I, shuv — the identical verb as v1's 'Return'] from them."

**Operation 1 — the LORD's own healing, free love, and turned anger.**
- **Action-type:** healed / loved freely / anger turned (three paired declarations, causally linked: love is possible because anger has turned)
- **Subject:** the LORD (first person throughout)
- **Operation:** state → state: apostasy (a condition) is healed; anger (a condition) has turned/departed; love (freely given) is the resulting orientation
- **Source:** self — the LORD's own declared decision, explicitly not conditioned on any further payment or merit beyond the confession just scripted (v2-3); "freely" (nedavah, voluntary-offering vocabulary) makes this point directly: the LORD's love is not a repayment for Israel's confession but a voluntary gift
- **Target:** Israel/Ephraim ("their," "them")

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Focused inner being — yes, directly and centrally: this verse is among the most explicit first-person interior-state declarations in the whole book (healing, free love, turned anger).
- Q3: Stated directly.
- Q4: Source — the LORD's own self, explicitly described as acting freely/voluntarily rather than as enabled by or conditioned on Israel's confession — a genuine state-vs-enablement distinction (Part B.5): Israel's confession (v2-3) is the occasion, but the LORD's love is declared "freely" given, not earned or caused by it.
- Q5: Target — Israel/Ephraim.
- Q6: State (turned anger, healed apostasy) resulting in a settled disposition (free love), not a single event.
- Q7: Linkage — this is the chapter's, and the book's, decisive answer to EQ26: v4's "my anger has turned [shuv] from them" uses the identical verb as v1's call for Israel to "return" [shuv] — a deliberate two-directional wordplay: Israel is called to turn back to the LORD (v1), and the LORD's own anger turns away from Israel (v4). Read together with ch11:8-9's earlier resolution ("my compassion grows warm and tender... I will not execute my burning anger... for I am God and not a man"), this verse extends and confirms that resolution as the book's final position, rather than reopening it — ch13:14's "compassion hidden" is best read, in light of this verse, as belonging to the judgment-oracle internal to ch13 (addressed to the still-unrepentant nation) rather than as this book's own final word, which is given here in ch14:4. This is treated as EQ26's resolution (see Emergent questions).
- Q8: Collective.
- Q9: Sufficient as stated.
- Q11: Action-type label — "healed / loved freely / anger turned" (three paired declarations).

**Decision.** Retain as stated IB operation — the book's clearest and most direct first-person statement of the LORD's own healed disposition, resolving EQ26 as this book's final position on the judgment/mercy tension.

### Hos 14:5

> I will be like the dew to Israel; he shall blossom like the lily; he shall take root like the trees of Lebanon;

**Observation.** The LORD's self-comparison to dew (H2919) — directly reversing ch13:3's use of "dew" as a figure for Israel's own transience ("they shall be like... the dew that goes early away") — now applied positively as the LORD's own life-giving presence. Israel is figured as blossoming (H6524A) like a lily and rooting (H8328) like Lebanon's trees.

**Operation 1 — the LORD as life-giving presence; Israel flourishes.**
- **Action-type:** became-source (the LORD as the enabling condition for Israel's flourishing — an enablement, not a state Israel achieves independently)
- **Subject:** the LORD (as dew) and Israel (as blossoming/rooting plant)
- **Operation:** come from/go to — the LORD's presence (dew) enables Israel's growth (blossom, root)
- **Source:** the LORD (explicitly named as the source/enabler of the flourishing — Part B.5's enablement category, distinct from a self-generated state)
- **Target:** Israel

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Focused inner being — indirectly, via agricultural figure; the flourishing stands for a restored relational/vital condition rather than naming an interior state directly.
- Q3: Stated directly via simile.
- Q4: Source — explicitly the LORD (enablement, not self-sourced flourishing).
- Q5: Target — Israel.
- Q6: Movement/state — the LORD's presence (dew, a recurring condition) enabling ongoing growth (blossom, root — states achieved through that enablement).
- Q7: Linkage — direct reversal of ch13:3's "dew that goes early away" (transience, applied to guilty Israel's own fate) — the identical image (dew) is repurposed from a figure of swift vanishing to a figure of the LORD's own sustaining presence; a clear before/after contrast bridging the book's judgment and restoration halves.
- Q8: Collective ("Israel," "he" as corporate singular).
- Q9: Sufficient as stated.
- Q11: Action-type label — "became-source" (dew, enabling growth).

**Decision.** Retain as stated IB operation — the LORD's own enabling presence, directly reversing the transience-figure used against Israel at ch13:3.

### Hos 14:6

> his shoots shall spread out; his beauty shall be like the olive, and his fragrance like Lebanon.

**Observation.** Continued flourishing imagery: shoots (H3127) spreading, beauty (H1935) like the olive, fragrance (H7381) like Lebanon — no new agent introduced; this verse elaborates v5's flourishing without further first-person divine speech.

**Operation 1 — continued elaboration of restored flourishing.**
- **Action-type:** flourished (continuing state, elaborated rather than newly asserted)
- **Subject:** Israel (continuing referent, "his")
- **Operation:** state — an ongoing condition of beauty and vitality
- **Source:** the LORD (continuing v5's enablement, though not re-stated explicitly in this verse — carried by context)
- **Target:** n/a (the flourishing is Israel's own resulting condition, not directed elsewhere)

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: No new interior state directly named; this verse elaborates the external/sensory figure (beauty, fragrance) of v5's flourishing.
- Q3: Stated directly via simile, continuing v5.
- Q4: Source — continuing from v5 (the LORD's enabling presence), not restated.
- Q5: N/a.
- Q6: State (elaborated flourishing).
- Q7: Linkage — continues v5's dew-reversal; no new cross-reference beyond the sustained agricultural figure shared with v5 and v7.
- Q8: Collective.
- Q9: Sufficient as stated.
- Q11: Action-type label — "flourished" (elaboration, continuing v5).

**Decision.** Recorded as referential aspect — this verse elaborates rather than introduces a new IB operation; retained as a continuation of v5's enabled flourishing.

### Hos 14:7

> They shall return and dwell beneath my shadow; they shall flourish like the grain; they shall blossom like the vine; their fame shall be like the wine of Lebanon.

**Observation.** "They shall return [H7725G, shuv again] and dwell [H3427] beneath my shadow [H6738]" — a direct answer to v1's opening call, now stated as accomplished/certain future rather than imperative. Further flourishing imagery follows (grain, vine, wine of Lebanon).

**Operation 1 — the called-for return realized; dwelling under the LORD's shadow.**
- **Action-type:** returned-and-dwelt (the fulfillment of v1's call, now stated as the LORD's own certain outcome)
- **Subject:** Israel/Ephraim ("they")
- **Operation:** come from/go to — a movement back (return) resulting in a settled state (dwelling under the LORD's shadow, i.e., protection/shade)
- **Source:** self (Israel's own returning act) enabled by the LORD (the shadow/shelter is the LORD's own provision)
- **Target:** the LORD ("beneath my shadow")

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Focused inner being — yes; "dwell beneath my shadow" names a relational condition of shelter/dependence, directly answering the interior reorientation called for at v1.
- Q3: Stated directly.
- Q4: Source — Israel's own returning act (self), resulting in dependence on the LORD's own provided shelter (enablement) — both are present and distinguished (Part B.5): the return is Israel's own movement; the shadow/shelter is the LORD's own gift.
- Q5: Target — the LORD.
- Q6: Movement (return) resulting in state (dwelling, sheltered).
- Q7: Linkage — directly closes the loop opened at v1's imperative "Return" — this verse states that call's own fulfillment, using the identical verb (shuv).
- Q8: Collective.
- Q9: Sufficient as stated.
- Q11: Action-type label — "returned-and-dwelt" (fulfillment of v1's call).

**Decision.** Retain as stated IB operation — the direct, verbally-marked fulfillment of the chapter's opening call to return.

### Hos 14:8

> O Ephraim, what have I to do with idols? It is I who answer and look after you. I am like an evergreen cypress; from me comes your fruit.

**Observation.** Direct rhetorical question addressed to Ephraim by name: "what have I to do with idols?" — a first-person repudiation of any continuing association with the idols named throughout the book (Baal, calves, ch13:1-2). Followed by self-identification: "It is I who answer [H6030B] and look after [H7789, the same root used of the LORD's predatory 'watching/lying in wait' at ch13:7, here repurposed positively] you... I am like an evergreen cypress [H1265]; from me comes your fruit [H6529]."

**Operation 1 — direct repudiation of idols; the LORD as sole source of fruit.**
- **Action-type:** repudiated (idols) / self-declared (as sole source of care and fruitfulness)
- **Subject:** the LORD (first person, addressing Ephraim directly by name)
- **Operation:** become evident — the LORD's own exclusive role (answering, watching over, fruit-source) is asserted directly against the idols just repudiated
- **Source:** self (the LORD's own declared identity and role)
- **Target:** Ephraim (addressed by name, "O Ephraim," "your fruit")

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Focused inner being — yes, directly: the LORD's own rhetorical self-examination ("what have I to do with idols?") and self-declared care ("answer and look after you") are explicit first-person interior/relational statements.
- Q3: Stated directly.
- Q4: Source — the LORD's own self, explicitly and finally repudiating any competing claim (idols).
- Q5: Target — Ephraim, named directly (the only verse in this chapter to use the tribal name rather than "Israel").
- Q6: State (self-declared identity) with a movement component (fruit "comes from" the LORD to Ephraim).
- Q7: Linkage — "look after" (H7789, shur) directly reuses the verb applied to the LORD's predatory lurking at ch13:7 ("like a leopard I will lurk beside the way") — the identical verb is repurposed from predatory watching to caring oversight, a striking verbal reversal marking the chapter's complete turn from judgment to restoration. Also: "fruit" (H6529) directly answers ch9:16/10:1's language of Ephraim's own fruit being struck down or self-directed, and connects to v2's "bulls"/fruit-of-lips wordplay tradition (noted, not adjudicated) — the LORD, not Ephraim's own idols or self-effort, is named as the true source of all fruit. This verse functions as the book's climactic direct repudiation of the idol-thread that opened at ch1-2 and recurred throughout (ch4:17, ch8:4-6, ch11:2, ch13:1-2).
- Q8: Individual-as-collective (Ephraim, the tribal name standing for the nation).
- Q9: Sufficient as stated.
- Q11: Action-type label — "repudiated idols / self-declared fruit-source."

**Decision.** Retain as stated IB operation — the book's climactic direct repudiation of idolatry and self-declaration of the LORD as sole source of care and fruitfulness, with a significant verbal reversal (shur, "watch/lurk") from ch13:7's predatory usage.

### Hos 14:9

> Whoever is wise, let him understand these things; whoever is discerning, let him know them; for the ways of the Lord are right, and the upright walk in them, but transgressors stumble in them.

**Observation.** Closing wisdom colophon, third-person and general (not addressed to Israel/Ephraim specifically): a call to the wise/discerning to "understand" (H0995) and "know" (H3045, yada — the book's own key relational-knowledge verb, here given a final, generalized wisdom-instruction usage) "these things"; a concluding maxim: "the ways [H1870G] of the LORD are right [H3477G]; the upright [H6662] walk [H1980I] in them, but transgressors [H6586] stumble [H3782] in them."

**Operation 1 — closing wisdom instruction; the two ways.**
- **Action-type:** instructed (a generalized, wisdom-genre closing appeal, distinct in register from the preceding first-person prophetic/relational material)
- **Subject:** an unnamed "whoever" (wise/discerning reader) and, within the maxim, "the upright" and "transgressors" as two contrasted classes
- **Operation:** state — two settled conditions (walking uprightly vs. stumbling) contingent on one's orientation to "the ways of the LORD," which are themselves declared "right" (an unchanging state, not a variable one)
- **Source:** self, for each class (the upright's walking and the transgressors' stumbling are both their own responses to the same "ways," which are constant)
- **Target:** n/a directly, though "the ways of the LORD" function as the shared reference-object both classes respond to differently

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Focused inner being — yes, generally: "understand," "know," "walk," "stumble" are all interior/behavioral-orientation terms, though addressed to an unspecified generalized reader rather than to Israel specifically.
- Q3: Stated directly, as a closing maxim.
- Q4: Source — each class's own response (upright walking, transgressors stumbling) to the constant "ways of the LORD"; the ways themselves are not sourced in the responder but are a fixed given.
- Q5: N/a (no specific external target; a general instructional statement).
- Q6: State (two contrasted, stable conditions).
- Q7: Linkage — "stumble" (H3782, kashal) directly closes the inclusio opened at v1's "you have stumbled because of your iniquity" — the chapter that opened with Israel's own specific stumbling closes with a generalized statement that transgressors (of any kind) stumble in the very ways that the upright walk in safely; this reframes Israel's own historical stumbling (v1) as one instance of a universal principle stated at the book's close. Also functions, in wisdom-literature style (cf. Ps 1's "two ways"), as a fitting envelope for the entire book's own extended case study in stumbling-then-called-return.
- Q8: Generalized/universal, not specifically corporate-Israel (a shift in address-register from the rest of the chapter).
- Q9: Sufficient as stated.
- Q11: Action-type label — "instructed" (closing wisdom colophon, two-ways framing).

**Decision.** Retain as stated IB operation (referential/framing) — a generalized closing maxim that completes the chapter's stumble/return inclusio (v1/v9) and reframes the book's entire case study in universal wisdom terms.

## Passage-level linkages (Q7)

1. **The stumble inclusio (v1/v9).** "You have stumbled" (v1, Israel specifically) and "transgressors stumble" (v9, generalized) bracket the whole chapter — kashal (H3782) opens and closes it.
2. **The shuv wordplay (v1/v4/v7).** "Return" (v1, Israel's called movement), "my anger has turned" (v4, the LORD's own movement), and "they shall return" (v7, the call's fulfillment) all use the identical root (shuv) — a deliberate three-fold structural device: Israel is called to turn (v1), the LORD's own anger turns away (v4), and Israel's return is realized (v7).
3. **The dew reversal (v5/ch13:3).** "Dew" as a figure for swift vanishing (ch13:3, applied to guilty Israel) is directly repurposed as the LORD's own sustaining presence (v5) — the same image inverted from judgment to restoration.
4. **The shur/"watch" reversal (v8/ch13:7).** The verb used of the LORD's predatory lurking ("like a leopard I will lurk," ch13:7) recurs at v8 in a caring register ("It is I who... look after you") — the identical verb repurposed from threat to care.
5. **The savior/save thread (v3/ch13:4,10).** Israel's own confession ("Assyria shall not save us") directly answers the LORD's prior assertions (ch13:4 "besides me there is no savior"; ch13:10's rhetorical "where is your king, to save you?") — confession finally aligning with the LORD's own prior diagnosis.
6. **The mercy/compassion thread and EQ26 (v3-4/ch13:14/ch11:8-9).** "The orphan finds mercy" (v3) and "my anger has turned... I will love them freely" (v4) together constitute this book's final resolution of the judgment/mercy tension raised at ch13:14 ("compassion is hidden") against ch11:8-9's earlier resolution — see Emergent questions.
7. **The fruit/idol reversal (v8/ch13:1-2, ch1-2, ch4:17, ch8:4-6, ch11:2).** "From me comes your fruit" directly repudiates the entire book's idol-thread in a single climactic first-person statement.
8. **Absence surfaced — Egypt is not named in this closing chapter**, though Assyria is explicitly renounced (v3); EQ23's Egypt/Assyria tension is therefore only partially engaged by the book's own ending (see Emergent questions).

## Insufficiencies register

- v2: the "bulls"/"fruit" of our lips text-critical question (Masoretic "bulls" vs. an alternate versional reading) is not resolved by the base extract's own data (which follows the Masoretic/ESV rendering); named as a known crux, not adjudicated here.
- v14 (ch13, for cross-reference): the racham (v3, this chapter) / nacham (ch13:14) root distinction is real — these are two different Hebrew roots within the same compassion/mercy semantic domain, not a single word's recurrence; the thematic reversal (hidden→found) is a content-level linkage, not a lexical-repetition one, and is presented as such above, not overstated as verbatim recurrence.
- v9: whether this closing colophon was composed as part of the original oracle or added as a later editorial frame (a live question in critical scholarship) is outside this base extract's data and is not adjudicated here; the debate treats it as it stands in the received text.

## Emergent questions log (filed against this passage — not merged across passages; resolved, if at all, at the whole-book read)

- **EQ26 (raised ch13, resolved here).** Ch13:14's "compassion is hidden from my eyes" is resolved by this chapter's v4 ("my anger has turned from them... I will love them freely") read together with ch11:8-9's earlier resolution: the book's own final position, stated in its closing oracle, is that the LORD's compassion/love prevails and anger is turned away — ch13:14's withholding is best understood as belonging to the judgment-oracle internal to ch13 (addressed to the still-unrepentant, idol-devoted nation depicted through vv1-12), not as the book's own final word, which this chapter supplies. Recommended resolution for the whole-book read: EQ26 RESOLVED — mercy is the book's final position, consistent with (not contradicting) ch13's own judgment material, understood as addressed to a different moment in the same relationship's arc.
- **EQ23 (Egypt/Assyria, carried from ch8-13) — partially engaged, not fully resolved.** V3 explicitly renounces Assyria as a source of security, directly closing that half of the tension; Egypt is not mentioned in this closing chapter at all. Whether the book's silence on Egypt at its close should be read as an implicit inclusion (Egypt renounced along with Assyria, by extension) or as a genuine gap the book itself never fully closes is carried to the whole-book read as the final open question on this thread.
- EQ27 (corporate guilt vs. non-culpable victims, ch13:16) — not addressed by this chapter's turn to restoration; remains open, carried to the whole-book read as a question the book itself does not appear to resolve within its own text.
